prompts.display_text: Pin the country, by today's borders, where a current Apostle was born.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country where a member of the First Presidency or the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles serving as of October 2026 was born.
prompts.note: Elder Uchtdorf's birthplace, Ostrava, is in today's Czech Republic.
prompts.summary: As of October 2026, President Dallin H. Oaks leads the Church, and the senior councils include leaders born outside the United States: Elder Uchtdorf in Ostrava (then Czechoslovakia), Elder Kearon in England, Elder Causse in France and Elder Soares in Brazil.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: President Oaks (Provo, Utah), President Eyring (Princeton, New Jersey), Elders Bednar, Gong, Gilbert, Rasband and others.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Elder Ulisses Soares, born in Sao Paulo in 1958.

answers.name: Czech Republic
answers.fact: Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf, born in 1940 in Ostrava, then Czechoslovakia.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Elder Patrick Kearon, born in Carlisle, England, in 1961.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: Elder Gerald Causse, born in Bordeaux in 1963.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country that Church History Topics lists for the area of Mischa Markow's missions.
prompts.text_original: Mischa Markow, one of the first converts in eastern Europe, served two missions in lands that today belong to several countries. Pin one of those present-day countries.
prompts.summary: Mischa Markow (1854-1934) was among the first Latter-day Saint converts in eastern Europe. Within 15 years of his conversion he served two missions across lands now in Hungary, Russia, Romania, Bulgaria, Turkey, Serbia, Croatia, Germany, Belgium and Latvia.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Named by Church History Topics among the countries of Markow's missions.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: Named among Markow's mission countries.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: Named among Markow's mission countries.

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Named among Markow's mission countries (Ottoman lands).

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: Named among Markow's mission countries.

answers.name: Romania
answers.fact: Named; he dreamed of preaching in Temesvar, now Timisoara, Romania.

answers.name: Serbia
answers.fact: Named among Markow's mission countries.

answers.name: Bulgaria
answers.fact: Named among Markow's mission countries.

answers.fact: Named among Markow's mission countries.

answers.name: Latvia
answers.fact: Named among Markow's mission countries.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country home to an Old Testament outsider the New Testament mentions (not Balaam, the queen of the south or Sodom)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country that was home to an Old Testament person or people from outside Abraham's family whom the New Testament mentions (not Balaam, the queen of the south or Sodom)
prompts.citation: Luke 4:26-27; Matthew 1:5-6; 12:41; Hebrews 7:1; 11:31; Romans 9:17; Galatians 4:24-25; 2 Timothy 3:8; 2 Samuel 11:3
prompts.note: Jericho is in the West Bank (PSE). Balaam's Pethor and the queen of the south's Sheba are disputed sites and are not counted.
prompts.summary: The New Testament keeps pointing to outsiders in Israel's story. Jesus praised Naaman of Syria, a widow of Sidon and the repentant Ninevites. Ruth of Moab and Rahab of Jericho appear in his genealogy, Melchizedek king of Salem in Hebrews, and Paul names Pharaoh, Hagar and the magicians of Egypt.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Paul names Pharaoh, Agar (Hagar the Egyptian), and the magicians Jannes and Jambres who withstood Moses (Romans 9:17; Galatians 4:24; 2 Timothy 3:8).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Jesus said the men of Nineveh, who repented at Jonah's preaching, would rise in judgment (Matthew 12:41).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Jesus recalled that Naaman the Syrian, of all the lepers, was cleansed (Luke 4:27).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Melchisedec was king of Salem, which the Bible Dictionary identifies with Jerusalem (Hebrews 7:1).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Ruth, a woman of Moab (Ruth 1:4), is named in Jesus' genealogy; Moab lay east of the Dead Sea (Matthew 1:5).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Jesus recalled Elijah being sent to a widow of Sarepta, a city of Sidon (Luke 4:26).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: By faith Rahab of Jericho, a Canaanite, perished not with them that believed not (Hebrews 11:31; Joshua 2).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Matthew 1:6 names Urias, Uriah the Hittite (2 Sam 11:3); the Bible Dictionary places the Hittites from the Orontes to the Euphrates, with an empire into Asia Minor.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose very first stake (a group of congregations) was organized between 1958 and 1962
prompts.text_original: Between 1958 and 1962 the Church organized its first stakes in a run of countries far from Utah, a sign that Saints abroad were being asked to build Zion where they lived. A country whose first stake of the Church was organized between 1958 and 1962.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (New Zealand, England, Australia, Netherlands, Germany, Switzerland, Samoa, Mexico)
prompts.note: Mexico does not count: its first stake, in the Chihuahua and Sonora colonies, came in 1895. Canada's also came in 1895.
prompts.summary: After New Zealand received its first stake at Auckland in 1958, stakes followed in Manchester, England and Sydney, Australia on the same day in 1960. Rotterdam, Berlin and Zurich gained the first stakes in the Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland in 1961, and Apia, Samoa followed in 1962.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: The Manchester England Stake, the first in Europe, was organized March 27, 1960.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: The first stake in Australia was organized in Sydney, March 27, 1960.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: The Berlin Germany Stake, the first in Germany, was organized September 10, 1961.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: The first stake in New Zealand was created in Auckland, May 18, 1958.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: The Zurich Switzerland Stake, the first in Switzerland, was organized October 27, 1961.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: The Holland Stake, the first in continental Europe, was created at Rotterdam, March 12, 1961.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: The first stake in the Samoan Islands was organized at Apia, Western Samoa, March 18, 1962.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where Jesus's family or his disciples fled or were sent to escape danger, in Matthew or Acts
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place where Jesus's family or his followers fled, or were sent, to escape danger, in Matthew or Acts
prompts.note: Antioch of Syria is today Antakya in Turkey, so it counts for Turkey, not Syria. Samaria is in the West Bank (Palestine).
prompts.summary: Danger kept scattering the faithful, and the gospel went with them. Joseph took Jesus into Egypt to escape Herod. After Stephen was stoned, disciples fled through Judea and Samaria and on to Phenice, Cyprus and Antioch. Paul was later rushed by night to Tarsus, Berea, Athens and Caesarea.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Joseph took the young child and Mary by night into Egypt to escape Herod (Matthew 2:13-14).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Joseph turned aside into Galilee; the brethren sent Saul to Caesarea, and soldiers took Paul there by night (Matthew 2:22; Acts 9:30; 23:23).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Saul was sent to Tarsus; scattered disciples reached Antioch; Paul and Barnabas fled to Lystra and Derbe (Acts 9:30; 11:19; 14:6).

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: Disciples scattered by the persecution over Stephen travelled as far as Cyprus (Acts 11:19).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: The brethren sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea, then brought Paul to Athens (Acts 17:10-15).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: After Stephen's death the church was scattered through Judea and Samaria (Acts 8:1).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: The scattered disciples also reached Phenice, the Phoenician coast of today's Lebanon (Acts 11:19).
